verdict.rationale: Framer documents real isolation primitives: external-agent changes automatically land on a branch that can be reviewed, undone or merged, branches keep the original project clean, and staging environments let you test on a framer.app domain before going live. This is true sandbox-style isolation, not just a dry-run. However, nothing explicitly says CMS data written by an agent (creates, updates, deletes) is isolated from production content, and there is no hands-on or independent confirmation. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that branch or staging isolation covers CMS/production data, a documented separate test-data sandbox, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: every change made by an external agent automatically happens on a branch. You can undo changes, review the branch, and decide when to merge it back into your main branch.
Staging environments. Test changes securely on a framer.app domain before pushing live.
Explore ideas in a branch without touching the main project. Merge when it’s ready to ship.
Work on a copy of your project and keep the original clean.
You stay in control of what gets published.
